scope: CPU/source observations and logical traffic models only. No measured speed or GPU-memory claim.

lora_epilogue.status: Pinned source and CPU checks plus logical traffic arithmetic; no physical GPU profiling
assumptions: All28 layers use maximum batch4x512 and q/v output widths1536/256.
Full-gradient upper bound; adapter-only first-block backward requires less original work.
Logical array reads/writes are not measured DRAM, allocator peak or runtime.
Native dropout and A/B GEMMs/retained activations remain unchanged.

rotary.status: CPU-observed operator counts plus arithmetic traffic model; not GPU profiling

cpu_observation.method: TorchDispatchMode over pinned eager apply_rotary_pos_emb and torch.autograd.grad; nested CPU torch.profiler confirms slice_backward zero-fill plus half-copy
cpu_observation.backward_excludes: leaf .grad storage allocation/copy; autograd.grad returns Q/K gradients directly

equations.R: FP32 round-to-nearest-even after each listed multiply and addition
equations.neg: exact sign-bit flip, including signed zero; not zero-minus
equations.Z: Z(z)=positive zero if z==0, otherwise z; reproduces slice-backward positive-zero padding
equations.coefficient_halves: c0,c1,s0,s1 are read independently; no duplicated-half assumption

traffic_basis.unit: N is total Q+K elements, each FP32 element is 4 bytes; coefficients excluded from the traffic table
traffic_basis.coefficient_logical_reads_if_counted: Add 8*N bytes to EACH direction for BOTH eager and fused; broadcast addresses repeat and are usually cacheable, so this is not unique DRAM volume.

launch_model.conditional_assumption: Treat each observed eager data operation as one CUDA launch; real CUDA cat/copy/fill dispatch must be profiled.

optional_first_layer_frozen_K_adjustment.condition: Only if first-layer K does not require a gradient (depends on actual input-gradient hooks).

validation.standalone_boundary_checks: exact finite values, scaled derivatives, distinct halves, tails, signed zeros, nonfinite classification, unusual upstream strides, optional/frozen gradients, alias/dispatch guards

limitations: Logical tensor-pass savings are an uncached upper-bound model of avoidable transfer. They are not measured DRAM bytes, peak-memory reduction, time, throughput, or a speedup prediction.
The 28-layer model assumes maximum sequence length and both gradients in every layer. Actual token lengths, frozen paths, dispatch choices, and cache reuse change the amount.

Forward tensors are transient. Neither reference nor fusion needs to save Q/K values for this frozen-coefficient backward; do not claim persistent per-layer Q/K activation savings or sum transient peaks over layers.

The custom autograd node can reschedule Q/K/V contributions to shared upstream hidden inputs even when Q/K have separate storage. Boundary exactness and the small CPU attention test do not prove whole-model bitwise parity.
The patch preserves FP32 Q/K, original meaningful layout, SDPA autocast, GQA replication/reduction, masks, attention scale, dropout, and RNG order. It does not fuse projections or trig generation.
Direct Q/K shared storage is guarded out. Trainable coefficients, unsupported shapes/layouts/dtypes/devices, and other unsqueeze dimensions delegate before custom work.

Physical T4 numerical tests, full-training metrics/gradients, event timings, sanitizer checks if needed, and the organizer measured-original-JIT-runtime gate remain outstanding. No claim of meeting the 5-percent eligibility threshold.
rotary.source_note: Pinned implementation contents were read from installed packages. NVIDIA PTX and official model config were also retrieved from the web. CPU profiler, not an unverified C++ source fetch, established nested slice-backward counts.
